nodes.label: Audit steps
nodes.rationale: Ordered events: model, tool, write, decision, card. Tool arguments are the highest-value field because most failures are wrong arguments that look like a correct reply. The decision event records minutes the user is never shown.

nodes.label: Evening Digest
nodes.rationale: At users.digest_hour, default 21, guarded by last_digest_on. Composed in code. Shipped without buttons because Fix one cannot carry an answer. Skipped on an empty day.

nodes.label: Seven-step Build Order
nodes.rationale: Riskiest infrastructure first, the free interaction path before the expensive one, and the planning ritual last once everything under it is proven. Each step leaves a check that can fail.

nodes.label: E2 Asymmetric Dedupe
nodes.rationale: An email that matches a chat row of the same amount in the last 60 minutes is discarded. A later chat entry attaches to a pending row of the same amount on the same day, unless two pending rows match, in which case neither is chosen. Every spend has one row: the bank supplies the amount and the user supplies the meaning.

nodes.label: E3 Digest Composed in Code
nodes.rationale: Listing rows and quoting amounts is not a judgement. A model should not do subtraction on money, the same reason A6 keeps budget arithmetic in code. The model is used only when the user replies.

nodes.label: A6 Budget Never Spoken
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic decides when to speak and is not itself reported. day_status returns week_is_full. The assistant may say the week is full and may not quote remaining minutes.

nodes.label: Groq Whisper
nodes.rationale: whisper-large-v3-turbo transcribes every Telegram voice note at about $0.04 per hour. Budgeted because Telegram does not include a transcript.

nodes.label: Reconciliation Flow
nodes.rationale: Triggered by the first planning act of a day, not by capture. Under or equal to 8 open items, one-by-one buttons; over 8, bulk Keep all / Drop all / One by one. Then challenge slips and speak about the week only qualitatively.

nodes.label: S1 Conversational Tasks
nodes.rationale: Add, update, and complete tasks by text or voice in phase 1a.

nodes.label: S2 Reconcile Yesterday First
nodes.rationale: Yesterday's list is reconciled before new tasks are accepted.

nodes.label: S3 Realistic in Time
nodes.rationale: Speak up when the week is full measured in time rather than task count, or when a task keeps slipping.

nodes.label: S6 Capture Never Blocked
nodes.rationale: Capturing a task is never blocked and never lectured. Friction lives at planning time.

nodes.label: slip_count
nodes.rationale: Times a task rolled over. Past slip_threshold (3) the assistant challenges whether it is real or should drop, instead of silently re-adding it.

nodes.label: weekly_budget_min
nodes.rationale: 720 minutes, Monday 00:00 local reset. Committed work counts, including completed work. Captured but unscheduled tasks do not, or capture would violate D8. Nothing rolls over as a bank.

nodes.label: Budgets Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: No users.budgets column and no overspend line. Metrics come after the foundation. Reversing it is one jsonb column and one line in the digest composer.

nodes.label: Architecture V1
nodes.rationale: Frozen why of V1. Foundation D1-D11 locked on 2026-09-12; supersedes the 2026-09-11 draft. The plan cites section numbers instead of re-deriving decisions.

nodes.label: D1 Voice Is a Message Type
nodes.norm_label: d1 voice is a message type
nodes.rationale: A voice note arrives on the same Telegram webhook as text. Download the ogg and send it to Groq whisper-large-v3-turbo; the rest of the pipeline is identical. Telegram does not ship a transcript the way the first WhatsApp draft assumed. A always-listening voice product is deferred.

nodes.label: D8 Capture Is Never Blocked
nodes.rationale: Blocking at capture loses the thought the product exists to keep. Capture onto the list is never lectured. Reconciliation and capacity apply only when committing onto a day. The nudge fires at most once per day via users.last_nudge_on. Brain dumps get one confirmation. Over about 8 unreconciled tasks, switch to bulk triage.

nodes.label: D9 Capacity Is Minutes
nodes.rationale: Category does not predict effort or urgency, so it must not gate the day. estimate_min and deadline_hard do. A hard deadline on a full week is added and then alerted, never refused. The weekly budget is 720 minutes, resets Monday 00:00 local, and is never spoken: day_status returns week_is_full. Capacity is a soft signal. Unscheduled captures do not consume the budget.

nodes.label: A4 Monday Local Reset
nodes.rationale: This week means Monday through Sunday. One constant if that assumption is wrong.

nodes.label: Agent2Agent Protocol
nodes.rationale: Delegation protocol between independent agents. A category error for in-process tooling. Token overhead cited at about 7 percent at 5 rounds and 23 percent at 10 rounds.

nodes.label: Fast Path
nodes.rationale: Deterministic callback payload such as done:task_id writes tasks and acks in about 100ms with zero tokens.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol
nodes.rationale: Transport for tools across a process or vendor boundary. Skipped until a client that is not this app needs the same tools.

nodes.label: Phase 1b
nodes.rationale: Gmail and the job-application spreadsheet were scoped as capability modules after the task store exists.

nodes.label: S4 Done Without an LLM
nodes.rationale: Mark a task done without paying for a model round trip.

nodes.label: S5 Gmail Deadlines Become Tasks
nodes.rationale: Deadlines from Gmail become tasks. Split into phase 1b so it cannot eat the core. Nothing in 1a is thrown away to add it.

nodes.label: sheets.py Job Spreadsheet
nodes.rationale: Deferred Phase 1b companion to Gmail: status-column updates from application emails. Not listed in the shipped README tree.

nodes.label: Phase 1b Poll Sketch
nodes.rationale: Original sketch: history.list every 15 minutes, a separate Claude call with its own context on claude-opus-5, and findings written as ordinary tasks with source gmail. Later plans replaced the cursor and the model call with a fixed window and regex.

nodes.label: D10 A2A Is Not Tooling
nodes.rationale: MCP connects an agent to tools; A2A connects agents to other agents. Adopting A2A would split capabilities into networked services and add large token overhead. A specialist context, such as Gmail extraction, is a function that makes its own model call, not a protocol. Revisit only for an agent you do not own.

nodes.label: D4 Fast Path Is the Default
nodes.norm_label: d4 fast path is the default
nodes.rationale: Inline-keyboard callbacks carry the task id, parse deterministically, and write the database with zero tokens. That is how a check-off avoids an LLM round trip. Roughly 40 percent of turns should land here, which is the main reason the bill stays near $13 rather than $30. A web app is not required for this.

nodes.label: G1 Fixed Window Not historyId
nodes.rationale: Gmail has no history on a first run and drops it after about a week, so the catch-up query exists anyway. A stored cursor is a second path whose failure is a silently skipped window. newer_than:2d every tick, deduped by email_events, is one path. An outage longer than two days loses the gap.

nodes.label: G3 Rules Not a Model
nodes.rationale: Both original lanes are fixed templates. A Claude call per email, as evaluation section 9 imagined, spends money on text a regex reads exactly. Unparsed outcomes are the extension point: add a pattern, or later send only those messages to a model.

nodes.label: V1 Non-goals
nodes.rationale: Multi-user UI, calendar, expenses, and a web app were non-goals for the first locked V1. Each was given a named seam and not built. Expenses later became Phase 1c against that seam.

nodes.label: Row Level Security
nodes.rationale: user_id plus an RLS policy from day one so a second human does not require a data migration. The bot uses the service_role key and bypasses RLS.

nodes.label: Expense kind
nodes.rationale: spend, refund, transfer, or cc_payment. transfer and cc_payment are stored and excluded from every spending total. cc_payment is a settlement of swipes already counted.

nodes.label: Gmail Privacy Boundary
nodes.rationale: Store the message id, sender, subject, and extracted scalars. Never store the body, snippet, HTML, OTPs, or full account numbers. The body is decoded, parsed, and dropped.

nodes.label: test_flow.py
nodes.rationale: Per-step assertions for rollover, natural-language capture, the fast path, the nag, the slip challenge, and the check-in. Also the production invariants run over real audit rows.

nodes.label: test_phase1.py
nodes.rationale: Offline checks for recurrence, expenses, the digest, and one end-to-end pass.

nodes.label: Evaluation Plan
nodes.rationale: Why every audit field exists, and the loop that turns a bad reply into a failing test. You cannot evaluate what you cannot replay.

nodes.label: Expense Tracking Plan
nodes.rationale: Phase 1c. Workflow settled 2026-09-13 and 2026-09-14. One capability file; core untouched. All five steps shipped, with two marked departures.

nodes.label: V1 Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Build order and per-step failing checks for Phase 1a. Holds the order of work; architecture holds the why.

nodes.label: README
nodes.rationale: V1 prototype status: code is built; the database migrations are the remaining hand step.

nodes.label: Log Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Never store email bodies, full card numbers, OTPs, API keys, or raw voice. Redact once at write time. Delete unlabelled audit rows after 60 days and keep labelled rows forever because those are the eval cases. Traces are a second copy of mail sitting behind service_role with no RLS.

nodes.label: E5 No SMS
nodes.rationale: SMS would need a forwarder with read access to every message, including OTPs, to buy latency a 21:00 digest does not need. Cash stays fully manual. Anything the bank only texts is never captured.

nodes.label: E7 kind Is Highest Risk
nodes.rationale: Reading a card-bill payment as a spend double-counts the month, silently. kind gets its own labelled set before the capability is trusted.

nodes.label: E9 Bill Is a Bound
nodes.rationale: The statement does not match captured spend exactly. Posting lag, auth versus settlement, un-alerted fees, refunds, and reversed authorisations are systematic gaps. A stable small delta is noise; a growing delta means alerts are not firing. This outside check exists only for the four credit cards.

nodes.label: A5 service_role Bypasses RLS
nodes.rationale: The bot server uses the Supabase service_role key. That key must never reach a browser.

nodes.label: Lane C Swipe Alerts
nodes.rationale: You spent $X mail writes a pending spend. Amount, card, and date count immediately; meaning stays blank until the digest.

nodes.label: E1 Extract on Arrival
nodes.rationale: The extract-on-arrival versus park-until-digest trade assumed extraction was a model call. Phase 1b showed the emails are a fixed template family, so regex runs on arrival, status pending carries the question, and nothing raw is stored.

nodes.label: channel_msg_id
nodes.rationale: Partial unique index. Telegram and WhatsApp retry webhooks, so processing a message twice is a database guarantee rather than careful application code.

nodes.label: due_on
nodes.rationale: The world's deadline, distinct from the day the work is planned. Conflating the two was a bug in the first draft.

nodes.label: last_nudge_on
nodes.rationale: One column so reconciliation is suggested at most once per day. Per-message nagging is what makes an assistant exhausting.

nodes.label: messages Table
nodes.rationale: Transcript plus token and cost metadata. channel_msg_id is the webhook retry guard.

nodes.label: planned_on
nodes.rationale: The day the user intends to do the task. Rollover operates on this column. A due date without a plan is an unscheduled deadline.

nodes.label: source_ref
nodes.rationale: Ingestion seam. Gmail-created rows are ordinary records with the message id, not a sync engine. Also the cross-mailbox dedupe key when prefixed by account label.

nodes.label: tasks Table
nodes.rationale: Owned by a user. planned_on is intent, due_on is the external deadline, estimate_min and deadline_hard drive capacity, slip_count drives the challenge.

nodes.label: users Table
nodes.rationale: One row per person. timezone defines today. weekly_budget_min, slip_threshold, last_nudge_on, and checkin_hour live here. auth_id stays null until a web app.

nodes.label: 004_email.sql
nodes.rationale: email_events ledger and applications table.

nodes.label: email_events
nodes.rationale: A row for every considered message, including ignore, parse failure, and error. Unique on (user_id, gmail_message_id). unparsed_* rows are the pattern backlog.

nodes.label: Webhook Idempotency
nodes.rationale: Insert messages with channel_msg_id first. A unique violation is a retry: return 200 and stop. Never 500 a webhook or Telegram will duplicate the work.

nodes.label: D5 Three Tables and JSONB
nodes.rationale: The schema is designed to be wrong. planned_on and due_on must not be conflated. meta jsonb holds experiments until they earn a column. user_id plus RLS from day one is not an accounts system. source plus source_ref is the ingestion seam. Migrations are ordered SQL files, not an ORM. channel_msg_id makes webhook retry idempotent in the database.

nodes.label: E4 One Message a Day
nodes.rationale: No immediate spend alerts. The planning nag exists because an assistant that interrupts twice stops being read. With budgets out of scope the digest reports and asks.

nodes.label: G12 Tokens Are Per-mailbox Env Vars
nodes.norm_label: g12 tokens are per-mailbox env vars
nodes.rationale: GMAIL_TOKEN_* is discovered by prefix. A JSON blob in one variable breaks because dotenv is sourced as a shell and braces expand. Stored ids are label:id because a Gmail message id is unique only inside one mailbox. Move to users.gmail_accounts when a second person uses this.

nodes.label: Fly.io Hosting
nodes.rationale: Webhook must be publicly reachable and always on, so a laptop is out. About $5 a month, deployed on day one.

nodes.label: mistral-small-latest
nodes.rationale: Single conversational and planning model in the locked cost table. Fast path uses no model. No prompt caching.

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres
nodes.rationale: System of record. Free tier is 500MB and pauses after 7 days of inactivity, which daily use and the cron make irrelevant.

nodes.label: Known Ceilings
nodes.rationale: Shipped routing is mistral-small-latest for both chat and the check-in, and cache_read_tokens stays 0. Blocking calls run in a thread, fine at one user. The 5-minute pending_question drop is specced and not built. python-dateutil was dropped in favor of zoneinfo and date.fromisoformat.

nodes.label: D7 Route Models by Path
nodes.rationale: Route by path, not intent classification. Button taps use no model. Conversational CRUD, rollover, and the 11am check-in use mistral-small-latest. Voice uses Groq whisper. Mistral does not support prompt caching so cache_read_tokens stays 0. Promote CHAT quality by changing one model name in core/turn.py. Supabase free tier pauses after 7 idle days; the daily cron prevents that.

nodes.label: G11 Raw REST over httpx
nodes.rationale: A refresh-token grant and two GETs, about thirty lines, using httpx already in requirements. The Google client library would have added six packages. requirements.txt stays unchanged.

nodes.label: A2 Python FastAPI Supabase Stack
nodes.rationale: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Supabase, and an Anthropic SDK tool runner, with claude-haiku-4-5 for chat and claude-opus-5 for planning. Reversal is expensive after Step 2. This vendor list disagrees with architecture D7, which specifies Mistral.

nodes.label: A3 Deploy Fly on Day One
nodes.norm_label: a3 deploy fly on day one
nodes.rationale: Hosting surprises found in week three are the expensive kind.

nodes.label: spent_at From the Alert
nodes.rationale: The transaction time in the email, not poll time. Using now() puts spending on the wrong day and, four times a year, the wrong month. Same rule as local_today: one helper.

nodes.label: applications Table
nodes.rationale: Keyed on company_key, not role. source_ref names the email that last moved the row and is not unique. An orphan rejection is still a row.

nodes.label: Lane B Job Applications
nodes.rationale: Receipts and rejections upsert applications as applied or rejected. Not interview invites.

nodes.label: test_gmail.py
nodes.rationale: Offline email-rule checks, including praise that must not classify as a rejection and the double-write checks.

nodes.label: Gmail Ingest Plan
nodes.rationale: Phase 1b shipped. Records settled seams so the next lane is an edit. No LLM call on the poll path.

nodes.label: G10 spent_at From the Email
nodes.rationale: Use the date stated in the payment confirmation. If the email names none, use Gmail internalDate. now() would drift with when the poll happened to run.

nodes.label: G2 Two Dedupe Layers
nodes.rationale: email_events (user_id, gmail_message_id) claims the message, including ignores and parse failures. expenses (user_id, source_ref) is the backstop, and a 23505 is success. applications has no unique source_ref because that column is overwritten with the email that last moved the row. The mailbox stays read-only; UNREAD is unused.

nodes.label: G4 Any Rejection Phrase Wins
nodes.rationale: Receipt alone is applied. Receipt plus rejection, or rejection with no receipt, is rejected. The third shape is the common email and a receipt-versus-rejection framing misses it. Body and subject are both scanned.

nodes.label: G5 Praise Guard Is an Absence
nodes.norm_label: g5 praise guard is an absence
nodes.rationale: Phrases like skills and background are impressive appear in rejections and in still-reviewing mail. REJECTION_PATTERNS matches the proceed/pursue/move-forward clause, and a test forbids praise phrases, instead of a combiner that undoes a bad entry.

nodes.label: G6 Key Applications on Company
nodes.rationale: Rejection mail often names a different role or none, so a (company, role) key would miss the row it exists to close. company_key drops punctuation and legal suffixes only. The index is not unique because applying twice to one company must stay possible.

nodes.label: G7 Orphan Rejection Becomes a Row
nodes.norm_label: g7 orphan rejection becomes a row
nodes.rationale: A rejection with no matching application is still inserted. A wrong row costs one correction; a dropped rejection is invisible. If no company can be extracted, the outcome is unparsed_application. Optimises recall, as evaluation section 9 asks.

nodes.label: G8 Sender Is a Hint
nodes.rationale: Gating Lane B on a noreply sender drops recruiter mail. Any receipt or rejection phrase routes to Lane B. The sender is still one rung of the company ladder, and ATS domains stop greenhouse.io being treated as the employer.

nodes.label: audit_log
nodes.rationale: One row per turn, written in a finally block. messages.meta is not enough because a turn that throws never reaches the assistant save, and those crashes are the turns most in need of an audit.

nodes.label: Capability Registry
nodes.rationale: Boot-time import of capabilities.*.TOOLS. About 15 lines. The SDK runner, not a custom loop, executes them.

nodes.label: meta JSONB
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch so a new field can be tried without a migration. Also holds pending_question until a column is earned.

nodes.label: pending_question
nodes.rationale: If the assistant asks for a missing deadline and hears nothing for 5 minutes, it drops the question and leaves the task undated. Stored as meta.pending_question.

nodes.label: Tool Search and defer_loading
nodes.rationale: Messages API feature, not an MCP feature. At roughly 20 tools, enable tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119 and defer low-frequency tools. At least one tool must stay eager or the API returns 400. Anthropic reported large accuracy gains and far fewer tool-definition tokens.

nodes.label: Scaling MCP Tools with Defer Loading
nodes.norm_label: scaling mcp tools with defer loading

nodes.label: D2 SDK Tool Runner Not MCP
nodes.norm_label: d2 sdk tool runner not mcp
nodes.rationale: There is no process or vendor boundary, so MCP portability is unused cost. Accuracy follows tool count in context, not protocol. Capabilities are Python functions on the SDK tool runner. Tool Search plus defer_loading is a later config flip near 20 tools. MCP is an export format only if an external client needs the tools. LangChain and a custom agent loop are skipped.

nodes.label: D3 Capability Is One File
nodes.rationale: A capability is one file exposing TOOLS and optional MIGRATIONS, JOBS, and PROMPT. Core discovers them with pkgutil and importlib. No plugin manifest, registry class, lifecycle hooks, or DI. Adding Gmail must not touch core.

nodes.label: Simplicity First
nodes.rationale: Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative: no extra features, single-use abstractions, or unrequested flexibility. The guidelines bias toward caution over speed.

nodes.label: Simplicity Pass
nodes.rationale: Applying guidelines section 2 to the draft. checkin_hour, a source CHECK for unbuilt capabilities, and week_summary() are speculative. auth_id plus RLS and meta jsonb are kept because they avoid a later migration and speculative columns.

nodes.label: amount
nodes.rationale: What the card was charged. Reconciles against the statement. Not expenditure, because subtracting a shrinking owed balance would make the same dinner cost more after friends repay.

nodes.label: expenses Table
nodes.rationale: One row per spend. Confirmed spends require a category. source is email, chat, or voice. source_ref is unique when present so one email cannot write two rows.

nodes.label: owed_amount
nodes.rationale: Outstanding to the user. Decrements as people repay and can reach zero. Independent of monthly expenditure.

nodes.label: share_amount
nodes.rationale: amount divided by headcount. The user's cost. Immutable when someone repays, which is why settlement must not recompute it.

nodes.label: 001_init.sql
nodes.rationale: Live draft of users, tasks, and messages, including partial indexes for open planned tasks and channel message ids.

nodes.label: 002_audit_log.sql
nodes.rationale: One audit row per turn, written from a finally block, with a GIN index on steps.

nodes.label: 003_expenses.sql
nodes.rationale: expenses table plus users.cards. Shipped with Phase 1b because card-bill payments needed a place to land.

nodes.label: 005_recurring.sql
nodes.rationale: Recurring reminders, applied after the email migration.

nodes.label: Expense Categories
nodes.rationale: Eleven values enforced by a CHECK: food, groceries, transport, housing, subscriptions, shopping, health, travel, entertainment, fees, other. food and groceries move independently. housing includes utilities. A card bill is not a category.

nodes.label: Migration Order
nodes.rationale: Apply 001 through 005 in the Supabase SQL editor. timezone must be a real IANA zone or rollover is silently wrong for part of each night. Then edit users.cards match strings to what the banks actually write.

nodes.label: evals/cases.jsonl
nodes.rationale: Frozen inputs and invariant expectations. The runner is a short loop calling handle_turn against a throwaway user. The trace table is the result store; there is no eval platform.

nodes.label: verdict
nodes.rationale: Hand label in the Supabase editor. The only ground truth. The triage query is verdict equals bad. If labelling takes more than ten seconds the loop dies.

nodes.label: Goal-Driven Execution
nodes.rationale: Turn each task into a verifiable check and loop until it passes. Weak criteria such as 'make it work' force constant clarification.

nodes.label: Surgical Changes
nodes.rationale: Touch only what the request requires. Match existing style, mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it, and remove only orphans your own edit created.

nodes.label: Think Before Coding
nodes.rationale: Do not assume or hide confusion. State assumptions, surface tradeoffs, and stop to name what is unclear before implementing.

nodes.label: Failure to Fix Loop
nodes.rationale: Mark verdict bad the same day, read steps rather than the reply, freeze an invariant in evals/cases.jsonl, fix the code or prompt the trace implicates, rerun the whole file, and promote a twice-failing case into test_flow.py. Assert invariants, never exact reply strings.

nodes.label: Card Configuration
nodes.rationale: Seven values including cash: amex_everyday, discover, chase_freedom, apple_card, chase_debit, sofi_debit, cash. Credit versus debit matters only so debit or cash cannot be a cc_payment and so reconciliation covers the four credit cards.

nodes.label: Lane A Card Bill Payments
nodes.rationale: Payment-confirmation emails write an expenses row with kind cc_payment and status confirmed. Checked before the spend family so a settlement is never read as a swipe.

nodes.label: E8 Cards Are Config
nodes.rationale: users.cards is the single source of truth: match strings, credit or debit or cash, and statement close day. No stored aggregate, because five write paths would drift and a wrong total looks authoritative. expenses.card is validated against the keys at write time so adding a card is not a migration. On a cc_payment row, card is the card being paid.

nodes.label: G9 Match Cards Only via users.cards
nodes.norm_label: g9 match cards only via users.cards
nodes.rationale: No second allowlist. Longest match string wins so Chase does not steal Chase Freedom. No match leaves card null and still writes the row: a wrong card corrupts reconciliation, a null card is visibly incomplete.

nodes.label: Phase 1a
nodes.rationale: Tasks, rollover ritual, fast path, and the 11am check-in. Builds the seam later modules drop into.

nodes.label: S7 11am Check-in
nodes.rationale: If the day has not been opened by 11am, the assistant opens it. This single feature moved proactive messaging into V1 and settled the channel.

nodes.label: Telegram Bot API
nodes.rationale: V1 channel. Free-form messages any time, buttons, and voice notes. Chosen because the 11am briefing cannot be a WhatsApp template.

nodes.label: WhatsApp Cloud API
nodes.rationale: Rejected for V1. Unprompted free-form text is outside the 24-hour window, and the window stops being free on 1 Oct 2026. Remains a one-day adapter if the template constraint is later accepted.

nodes.label: LLM Judge for the Briefing
nodes.rationale: Only the 11am briefing has no equality invariant. A judge everywhere else would add cost and nondeterminism. Add it after about twenty labelled briefings, not before.

nodes.label: D11 Channel Is Swappable
nodes.rationale: Adopt WhatsApp limits now so Telegram-only features do not have to be undone: at most 3 buttons, labels at most 20 characters, payloads at most 64 bytes, plain text, and never edit a sent message. handle_turn returns a reply object and app.py sends it. Nothing outside core/channels may import a channel module.

nodes.label: D6 Telegram Not WhatsApp
nodes.rationale: The 11am check-in fires when the user has not been in the chat, which is outside WhatsApp's 24-hour window. A pre-approved template cannot carry a briefing composed that morning. Telegram allows free-form proactive text. Hosting is Fly.io from day one because a webhook must stay public. Proactive messaging is the same handle_turn with a cron caller, not a second pipeline. Job queues are skipped.

nodes.label: E6 Splits Are Chat Only
nodes.rationale: A bank email cannot know a dinner was split. Buttons cannot carry an amount under the D11 payload and label caps, so there is no split button.

nodes.label: A1 Telegram for V1
nodes.rationale: Same channel call as D6. Reverse cost is one adapter and a fixed-shape 11am template; nothing else changes.

nodes.label: Open Items O4 O7 O10-O12
nodes.rationale: None block Step 0. Web app may stay read-plus-checkoff. checkin_hour may be hardcoded later. The real-deadline line is corrected in passing. drop_task always confirms. A per-day budget override needs users.meta.
